audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL-focused specs (EIP-8123 gas cap query, EIP-7823 MODEXP bounds, Prague EOA delegation EIP-7702, EIP-4788 beacon root storage, EIP-7808 tx type namespace, Cancun trie, numeric utilities, genesis block creation) plus networking (EIP-627 Whisper) and browser-side wallet discovery (EIP-6963).

in_scope: Beacon root provision to EL via Engine API

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EL component - the RPC node providing eth_txGasLimitCap is part of the EL node itself, not an external entity
Internal EVM component - contract or EOA calling MODEXP precompile is within the EL execution context
Internal to node - Whisper application layer is part of the node software, not an external data source
Internal EVM component - contracts querying beacon roots are within the EL
Duplicate of EXT-CONSENSUS-LAYER - same entity described twice
Internal EVM component - gas calculation is part of the EL execution engine
Internal EL component - fee market calculation is part of block processing
Internal utility - cryptographic operations are internal to the EL
Internal validation component - numeric validation utilities are internal to the EL

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Gas Cap Query / TX Submission)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users query gas caps and submit transactions via unauthenticated JSON-RPC. Malicious nodes could return incorrect cap info; malicious users can submit arbitrary transactions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Attacker via MODEXP Precompile Input
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: CALL to precompile address 0x05 with oversized input data
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any transaction can call the MODEXP precompile with arbitrary input. EIP-7823 adds 1024-byte bounds to prevent consensus bugs from large inputs. All input is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Whisper P2P Peer via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers send envelopes with potentially malformed structures, invalid PoW, or expired messages. All peer data requires full validation. Disconnect on severe violations.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via SET_CODE Transaction (EIP-7702)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit EOA delegation transactions. Authorization signatures must be cryptographically verified. Chain ID, nonce, and existing code checks provide multi-layer validation. Forged signatures must be rejected.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API (Beacon Root)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API - parent_beacon_block_root in block header (EIP-4788)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL provides beacon block roots via authenticated Engine API (JWT). EL unconditionally trusts the root's authenticity but must validate the system call execution. If CL is compromised, EL inherits that compromise.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Submitter (L1/L2)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission with RIP-range type bytes (0x40-0x7f) per EIP-7808
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction submitters may use L2-specific RIP transaction types. L1 nodes must correctly route or reject unknown types. No authentication on transaction type.

trusted_external_entities.name: L2 Rollup System
trusted_external_entities.rationale: L2 rollups define custom transaction types within reserved namespace. L1 should not process RIP types as EIP types. No trust relationship between L1 and L2 type definitions.

trusted_external_entities.name: Genesis Configuration File
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: JSON configuration file in assets/ directory
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Genesis configuration defines initial state including account balances. A tampered genesis file could pre-allocate funds to attackers. File integrity must be verified against known hashes.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet Browser Extension via DOM Events
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Browser extensions inject code and announce providers. Malicious extensions can impersonate legitimate wallets, inject fake providers, or attempt prototype pollution. Object.freeze() and img-tag SVG rendering provide mitigations.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Browser Extension
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Browser page context injection, eip6963:announceProvider spoofing
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious extensions can impersonate wallets, inject SVG with scripts, or perform prototype pollution. All extension-provided data is untrusted. DApps must freeze objects and render SVG safely.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Node computes min(protocolCap, policyCap). Response integrity depends on node honesty. Clients should not blindly trust returned values from untrusted RPC endpoints.
All three length parameters (BASE, EXPONENT, MODULUS) must be <= 1024 bytes. Violation consumes all gas and returns error. Length check must happen before complex pricing calculation.
Full envelope validation required: structure, PoW, bloom filter match. Invalid PoW (NaN, INF, negative) must be rejected. Severe violations trigger peer disconnect.

ECDSA signature validation (y_parity, r, s ranges), chain ID check, nonce match, existing code validation. Invalid authorizations silently skipped. 0xef0100 marker must uniquely identify delegation code.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: parent_beacon_block_root in block header, system call to beacon roots contract (EIP-4788)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Root authenticity guaranteed by CL. System call uses 30M gas (not from block limit). Ring buffer at index = timestamp % 8191. Timestamp validation prevents stale queries.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction type byte parsing and namespace routing (EIP-7808)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Types 0x40-0x7f reserved for RIP. L1 must not process unknown RIP types. Correct namespace boundary enforcement required for cross-layer compatibility.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Genesis block initialization from JSON config
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Genesis file integrity must be verified. All hex values must be parsed correctly. Account addresses must be valid 20-byte values. Chain ID must match expected network.
Provider detail must be Object.freeze()'d. UUID must be UUIDv4. RDNS must be valid RFC-1034. SVG icons must be rendered via img tag only. Duplicate UUIDs indicate tampering.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Browser page context, eip6963:announceProvider event spoofing
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Object.freeze() prevents prototype pollution. SVG via img tag prevents script execution. DApps must not trust rdns or icon as authentication. Users must verify wallet identity through external means.

coverage_gaps.reason: L2 rollup as a governance entity defining RIP types is covered indirectly through EXT-TX-SUBMITTER-L2 boundary edge. No direct data flow edge from L2 governance to EL.
